52 Years of Refusing toGive Up on Rural Education

The Problem We Exist to Solve

Wardha, 1973 — And Still Today

Wardha district, eastern Maharashtra. One of India's most educationally underserved regions.

Villages where the nearest school is 10 kilometres away. Families where no one has ever held a degree. Girls who are married at 17 because there is no hostel near their college. Boys who drop out at 14 because hunger is more urgent than homework.

This is where Chetana Education Society has worked — every single day — for 52 years.

"Education is not something we give to children.It is something we owe them — and we have been paying that debt, one institution at a time, since 1973."
— Chetana Education Society · 52 years of uninterrupted service in rural Wardha, Maharashtra
Our Beginning

One Man. One Conviction. Seven Institutions.

Shri Dinesh Baliram Sawai
Founder President · CES, 1973

In 1973, Shri Dinesh Baliram Sawai — an educationist from Wardha's historically marginalised community, with no resources but absolute conviction — founded Chetana Education Society.

His belief was radical for its time: every child deserves quality education regardless of family income, caste, or village. He started with one institution. Today, five decades later, there are seven — and over 35,000 students have walked through their doors.

"We did not wait for government. We did not wait for funding. We built — one institution at a time."

Our Journey

53 Years of Building, One Institution at a Time

1973
CES Founded by Shri Dinesh Baliram Sawai
Trust Reg. F/164/1973 · One institution, one conviction.
1990
D.Ed College Established
Teacher training begins — a profession for women who had none.
1993
Three Institutions in One Year
Dr. Ambedkar College of Social Work · Jotirao Phule College · Amrapali Girls' Hostel
1994
Ramdas Magaswargiy Boys' Hostel
Free food, shelter, care for boys from farming families — 30+ years uninterrupted.
2007
Chetana B.Ed College
60%+ women students · RTMNU affiliated
2011
Chetana ITI
NCVT-affiliated · Electrician, Fitter, Motor Repairing
2013
Oxford Public School & Junior College
750 students · 30+ farming villages · Asmita Ganvir → IIT Guwahati
2022
Chetana Institute of Pharmacy
D.Pharm · MSBTE affiliated · Rural women in science
2026 · Latest
International MoU — Dhammakaya Foundation, Thailand
CES's first international partnership · Signed April 2026 by Dr. Chetana Sawai
April 2026 · Thailand

CES Signs MoU with Dhammakaya Foundation, Thailand

In April 2026, CES signed a Framework MoU with the Dhammakaya Foundation — one of Asia's most respected humanitarian organisations — marking CES's first international partnership.

"On the same evening, six Oxford Public School girls from Wardha won international scholarships in Thailand. Two recognitions. One message: rural Maharashtra can compete with the world."

What We Stand For

Our Values — Rooted in Maharashtra's Tradition of Reform

📚
Education as a Right
Every child deserves quality education regardless of income, caste, village, or gender. Not a philosophy — the operating principle behind every decision we make.
🌾
Rural-First, Always
We have always been, and will remain, rooted in rural Wardha. We serve the villages that others pass through on the way to somewhere else.
⚖️
Phule-Shahu-Ambedkar Tradition
Our work is rooted in Maharashtra's tradition of social reform — education as liberation for marginalised communities.

52 years of proof.
